title: Sets and membership

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. Stories and worked quantities are originally authored constructed examples, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate evidence before publication.
purpose: Choose membership rules and see exactly which objects remain in a set.
meaning: A set is a collection of distinct objects with a well-defined membership rule. The live specimen compares two finite subsets of one universal set, showing intersection, union and ordered difference while keeping the resulting set separate from its cardinality.

definition.setting: Finite sets of distinct labeled objects; the live universe consists of twelve candidate peg heights.
definition.formal_latex: U=\{1,2,\ldots,12\},\quad A=\{u\in U:u\le a\},\quad B=\{u\in U:u\ge b\},\quad R\in\{A\cap B,A\cup B,A\setminus B\},\quad output=|R|.

signature.U: Fixed set of candidate labels 1 through 12.
signature.A,B,R: Finite sets of labels, not scalar counts.

conditions: The universal set is the fixed finite collection U={1,2,...,12}; each label denotes one distinct candidate peg with that height in centimetres.
A contains the members u of U with u<=maxSize, and B contains the members u of U with u>=minSize. Both inequalities include equality.
The chosen result R is intersection, union or ordered difference A∖B. Inclusive OR includes membership in either or both sets; difference removes B members from A.
The primary output |R| is cardinality: a whole number of members, not the length of a continuous interval or the sum of peg heights.
Continuous cutoff motion changes membership only when a fixed candidate height is crossed. A partially crossed drawing does not create a fraction of a member.
At an exact shared integer cutoff the intersection can be a singleton with cardinality one; an empty set has cardinality zero.
The finite-union identity is |A∪B|=|A|+|B|−|A∩B|, counting each distinct member once.
definition.domain_notes: General set theory includes finite and infinite sets and many kinds of objects. This specimen only filters the fixed twelve labeled heights. It is not a measure of interval length, a multiset with duplicate entries, or an automatic proof checker.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level references; restricted-family properties are author-derived. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: U=\{1,2,\ldots,12\},\quad A=\{u\in U:u\le a\},\quad B=\{u\in U:u\ge b\},\quad R\in\{A\cap B,A\cup B,A\setminus B\},\quad output=|R|.
grammar.formation_rule: U={1,2,...,12}; A={u∈U:u<=maxSize}; B={u∈U:u>=minSize}; R=A∩B for intersection, A∪B for union, A∖B for difference; output=resultCount=|R|.
grammar.precedence: Evaluate both membership predicates on the same universe, apply the selected set operation, then count distinct resulting members. A∖B is ordered and need not equal B∖A.

parse_errors.input: Treat |R| as the length between two cutoffs
parse_errors.reason: Cardinality counts selected fixed objects; an interval length measures a different quantity.

parse_errors.input: Replace A∩B by A∪B without changing the question
parse_errors.reason: AND requires both rules; inclusive OR accepts either or both.

parse_errors.input: Call an empty result a set containing zero
parse_errors.reason: The empty set has no members; a set containing the number zero has one member, and zero is not a candidate here.

grammar.ast_coverage: A narrow typed expression outline for the declared executable specimen. Function references name fixed finite selection/counting procedures; no general set parser, statistical inference engine or program analyzer is claimed.

properties.claim: Finite union avoids counting the intersection twice.
properties.conditions: A and B are finite subsets of the same universe.
properties.derivation: Count the A-only, shared and B-only membership groups once each.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

properties.claim: A singleton can occur at equal inclusive cutoffs.
properties.conditions: The shared cutoff is one of the candidate integer heights.
properties.derivation: That one height satisfies both <= and >=; cardinality is one despite zero cutoff separation.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

properties.claim: Raising a maximum cutoff cannot remove an intersection member when the minimum is fixed.
properties.conditions: Use intersection and hold the candidate universe and minSize fixed.
properties.derivation: Every previously accepted u still satisfies u<=the larger maximum and the unchanged minimum.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

prompts.prompt: Can a count change smoothly between four and five members?
prompts.answer: Not for this finite distinct collection. The threshold band can move smoothly, but the cardinality changes when another fixed candidate enters.

prompts.prompt: Why is equal cutoff separation not an empty set?
prompts.answer: The inclusive rules can share a candidate at that exact height. Cardinality counts that object, not the gap length.

representations.description: Fixed candidate labels, moving inclusive cutoff bands, the sets A and B and the selected result R connect membership predicates with actual accepted objects.
Cardinality is plotted against the maximum cutoff at fixed minimum and operation. The graph preserves discrete changes rather than inventing fractional members.
Roster lists and the cardinalities of intersection, union and ordered difference are evaluated from the same twelve candidates.
